sections.h2: Who keeps property records in Williamson County, Texas?
sections.html:
The Williamson County Clerk keeps them. Deeds, liens, releases of liens, plats, restrictions, trusts and similar instruments go into the Official Public Records the clerk maintains.

The same office also runs the probate court clerk's work, the commissioners court clerk's work and local birth, marriage and death registration. For a seller, the part that matters is land recording, because every deed, deed of trust release and lien notice that touches a Williamson County house lands there.

  • Land recording and vital records counter: 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, TX 78626.
  • Court filings: the Justice Center, 405 Martin Luther King St., Georgetown.
  • Phone: 512-943-1515. Mailing address: PO Box 647, Jarrell, TX 76537-0647.
  • Hours at the Research Library, Recording and Vitals counter: 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday. Courts keep 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The county clerk page says staff do not perform searches for the public, citing Attorney General Opinion WW-607, and cannot give legal advice. Plan on running your own search or asking a title company to do it.

sections.h2: How do I search Williamson County property records?
sections.html:
Use the clerk's Search Records page, which links to an Official Public Records Search, a judicial records search and a link for military discharge records.

Start with the owner name from your deed or tax bill, then look for anything recorded after it: a deed of trust, a release of lien, an abstract of judgment, a notice of foreclosure sale or an affidavit. A release that was never recorded is the most common reason a lien still shows against a house the owner thinks is paid off. If you find one, the lender has to record a release in the same office, because Local Government Code 192.007, as quoted on the clerk's site, requires any action on a recorded instrument to be made by recording another instrument in the same manner.

The county also posts a map viewer and links to the Williamson Central Appraisal District for ownership and value. Ownership on the appraisal roll can lag the deed records, so treat the clerk's records as the source for who holds title.

sections.h2: What does Texas require before a deed can be recorded here?
sections.html:
The instrument must be signed and acknowledged, or sworn to before two subscribing witnesses, before an officer authorized to take acknowledgments (Property Code 12.001(b), as summarized in the Texas Courts county clerk manual).

The clerk records deeds in the county where the land sits, so a Williamson County house is recorded in Georgetown no matter where the owner lives. Williamson County's fee page adds that a current photo ID must accompany the document and the fee, citing House Bill 1195 from the 88th Legislature.

Deed records the manual lists include general warranty, special warranty, quitclaim, trustee's, sheriff's and tax deeds, plus affidavits, releases of deeds of trust, leases, contracts of sale and powers of attorney. Recording does not make a defective deed valid. It gives public notice of what the paper says.

sections.h2: What does recording a document cost?
sections.html:
The clerk's current schedule is the Williamson County 2024 Recording Fees PDF on the Fees page. The state manual below is the statutory base, so confirm the county total before you send a check.

Texas county clerk recording fee structure (2023 County Clerk Manual, Texas Courts)
ChargeAmount printed in the manual
First page$5.00
Each added page, part page or attachment$4.00
Each name over five indexed$0.25
Records management and preservationNot more than $10
Records archiveNot more than $10
Records technology and infrastructure$2.00

A deed with no grantee mailing address can draw an added charge of $25, per the same manual. A commissioners court may direct the clerk to waive real property recording fees for buyers using certain grant programs, so ask the clerk whether Williamson County has done so.

sections.h2: How can an owner guard against a fraudulent deed or lien?
sections.html:
Sign up for Property Fraud Alert, which the clerk's page describes as a free service that emails or calls you whenever a document is recorded under a name you request.

If a judgment lien or conveyance looks fraudulent, the county's page lays out four steps through the District Clerk.

  • File a petition with the District Clerk.
  • File an Owner's Affidavit of Purported Conveyance.
  • Wait while a district judge reviews and signs findings of fact and conclusions of law.
  • File a certified copy of the signed order with the County Clerk in the Official Public Records, which the page says costs nothing.

The page cites Government Code 51.902 and 51.903 for this process and suggests asking the District Clerk about a temporary restraining order. Get legal advice before filing.

sections.h2: Where do foreclosure notices and sales happen in Williamson County?
sections.html:
The county's foreclosure and trustee sale page says sales are held on the first Tuesday of each month outside the Justice Center at 405 MLK Street in Georgetown.

Texas State Law Library guidance says the lender's notice of sale goes out at least 21 days before the sale, is posted at the courthouse door and is filed with the county clerk. A borrower who gets a notice of default may reinstate by paying the past due amount within 20 days of receiving it.

If a notice is recorded against your house, the clerk's records will show it. Selling before the sale date is possible, and the payoff then comes from the sale at closing. Ask a title company for a payoff figure rather than estimating it.

sections.h2: How do I record transfers after a death in Williamson County?
sections.html:
Which paper you record depends on the route. The State Law Library lists several: an affidavit of death with a death certificate for a transfer on death deed, an executor's or administrator's deed for an administered estate, a court order and will for a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship.

The probate side of the same clerk's office handles applications and small estate affidavits. A small estate affidavit under Estates Code chapter 205 requires no will, assets of $75,000 or less excluding homestead and exempt property, and court approval. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the clerk, and no law forces a buyer or title company to accept it.

The county cannot add heirs to an old deed. Whoever takes title records the proving paper, then the sale deed follows.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Williamson County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 752,827 residents in Williamson County as of July 2025, up 23.6 percent from the April 2020 base, in about 1,116 square miles of land.

Owners occupy 66.4 percent of housing units, and the 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes is $447,000. Median gross rent is $1,796. The county issued 4,956 building permits in 2025, which tells you new construction competes with resale listings.

Fast growth means many houses changed hands recently and sit under recent deeds and loans, which makes the record search quick. Older rural parcels, inherited homes and houses with unreleased liens are the ones that need paper cleanup before closing.

faqs.q: Does the Williamson County Clerk run searches for me?
faqs.a: No. The clerk's page says the office does not perform searches for the public, citing Attorney General Opinion WW-607. Use the online Official Public Records Search or ask a title company.

faqs.q: Do I need ID to record a deed in Williamson County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Fees page says a current photo ID must accompany the document and the fee, per House Bill 1195 from the 88th Legislature.

faqs.q: Where can I find the exact recording fee?
faqs.a: On the clerk's Fees page, which links the 2024 Recording Fees PDF. The 2023 state manual gives $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page as the base.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Williamson County house with a lien on it?
faqs.a: Often yes, if the lien is paid from the sale at closing. A title company can pull the recorded lien, request a payoff and handle the release. Ask the clerk or a title company if a release was never recorded.

faqs.q: Is the county clerk the same office as the tax office?
faqs.a: No. The county tax assessor-collector and the Williamson Central Appraisal District are separate offices. The clerk records documents and keeps probate and commissioners court records.
